questions.q: Convert for a message: 'Tell Rahul that I said, "I will bring the book tomorrow".'
questions.a: 'Ravi called — he said he would bring the book tomorrow/the next day.' A wrong answer keeping 'I will bring' inside the message shows direct-speech leak — messages report, they don't quote.

questions.q: What are the five elements of a message format?
questions.a: Date, time, receiver's name/salutation, the reported message body, writer's name. A wrong answer missing date/time shows the student treats messages like mini-letters.

questions.q: A message reads 85 words and includes 'Hello! How are you? It was such a nice chat.' — what's wrong?
questions.a: Word-limit breach plus conversational filler — a message relays facts for action, not the chat. A wrong answer 'it's fine' shows the student doesn't know messages are clipped instruments.

questions.q: A message is a compressed ______ record: when the writer wasn't there, you relay what matters — date and time of writing, the caller's name, the actual message in clipped sentences, and your name.

Fill in the blank: A message is a compressed ______ record: when the writer wasn't there, you relay what matters — date and time of writing, the caller's name, the actual message in clipped sentences, and your name.

Fill in the blank: The relay test: read a ______, extract what the RECEIVER must know — who called, about what, what action is needed, when. 'Anil called — your cricket kit is at his house; collect it before 6 pm.' Time-stamp at top, signature at bottom, box if required.
Fill in the blank: About ______ words, indirect speech, no decoration.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student compresses a telephone/verbal exchange into a ≤50-word message with all five elements, converting direct quotes to reported form.
